name: Equaerillon Duskwalker Variant

body:
Some rare duskwalkers appear to draw some influence from aeons or other, more mysterious beings, rather than just psychopomps. Like their more common duskwalker kin, they appear spontaneously as (roughly) 8-year-old children; instead of a place connected to death, however, an equaerillon usually appears in a temple or consecrated area of a neutral faith dedicated to balance and nature.

An eqaerillon’s appearance often differs from that of a standard duskwalker—their skin may have a metallic sheen, or their eyes may swirl with mystical color, for example.

Like common duskwalkers, they are usually Neutral in their outlook, but eqaerillons are more concerned with maintaining the balance and harmony of the Multiverse.

Core Traits
Ability Scores You gain +2 Con, +2 Wis, –2 Dex. This alters ability scores.
Protect the Balance Once per day, you can use your choice of protection from chaos, protection from evil, protection from good, or protection from law as a spell-like ability. You make this choice each day as you use this spell-like ability. You use your character level as the caster level, and Charisma as your casting ability score. When you reach 4th level, you can instead use this ability as magic circle against chaos, magic circle against evil, magic circle against good, or magic circle against law. This trait replaces ghost hunter.
Ward Against Disruption Traits You gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against emotion and fear effects. In addition, you gain a +4 species bonus to your CMD against any attack that would attempt to move you from your space, such as a bull rush or reposition maneuver. This trait replaces ward against corruption.
Favored Class Bonuses

For most of the duskwalker’s favored class bonuses, see Paizo’s player guide for plane hoppers (page 17). The following additional options are available to duskwalkers who have the listed favored class.

Druid Add +1/2 to the damage dealt by your animal companion’s natural attacks against undead.
Shaman Add one spell from the wizard’s necromancy school spell list that isn’t on the shaman spell list to your shaman spell list. This spell must be at least one spell level below the highest-level shaman spell you can cast.
